name: Niejuan
current_role: Co-founder and co-controlling shareholder (with husband Zhang Min) of Cofoe Medical Technology (可孚医疗, SZ:301087); stepped down as vice chair in Jan 2023
profile: Nie Juan (聂娟) co-founded the home-medical-device business that became Cofoe with her husband Zhang Min, starting with predecessor brand 'Haohushi' (好护士) in 2007. Cofoe (blood-pressure monitors, hearing aids, wheelchairs, consumables) listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2021; the couple jointly control it. She resigned as vice chair in January 2023 and is no longer an executive.
interesting_fact: Cofoe grew out of Zhang Min distributing blood-pressure monitors, wheelchairs and cupping devices before he finished junior college; at about 30 he created the Cofoe brand and moved from distribution into own-brand manufacturing.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding the business, Nie Juan was a government employee: a clerk at the Yiyang Municipal Engineering Management Office (益阳市市政工程管理处) in Hunan.
notes: Low public profile; not an executive since 2023. Best route is Cofoe's board-secretary office (secretary Xue Xiaoqiao) via the IR email; husband Zhang Min is chairman/president.

name: James Peng
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Pony.ai (Nasdaq: PONY; also listed in Hong Kong)
profile: James Peng (Peng Jun) co-founded robotaxi company Pony.ai in late 2016 with fellow ex-Baidu engineer Tiancheng Lou, after 11 years at Google and Baidu, where he was chief architect of autonomous-driving R&D. Pony.ai listed on Nasdaq in Nov 2024 and later added a Hong Kong listing; it runs driverless robotaxi services in Chinese megacities such as Guangzhou, Beijing and Shenzhen and is mass-producing its Gen-7 robotaxis.
interesting_fact: Peng holds a Tsinghua undergraduate degree, an MS from the University at Buffalo and an engineering PhD from Stanford, and spent seven years at Google building back-end and front-end advertising systems before moving into self-driving.
deep_cut_fact: He was Baidu's first US-based AI hire: Baidu SVP Wang Jing invited him to start Baidu Research US, and he was promoted to chief architect for autonomous driving in 2015 before leaving at the end of 2016 to found Pony.ai.
notes: Highly relevant to an energy/data-center/AI podcast (autonomous driving compute). He speaks publicly fairly often (Fortune Mar 2026 interview). media@pony.ai appears in 2025 releases; recent releases list only ir@pony.ai. Fortune: https://fortune.com/2026/03/26/pony-ai-ceo-james-peng-china-robotaxi

name: Zhang Buzhen
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, YSB Inc. (药师帮, HKEX: 9885), Guangzhou
profile: Zhang Buzhen (张步镇) spent about 15 years at SouFun (搜房网, now Fang.com), rising to CTO and then VP in charge of web, technology, product and mobile. He then applied the internet-platform model to China's fragmented drug-distribution market, founding Guangzhou-based YSB, a B2B platform linking pharmaceutical wholesalers with grassroots pharmacies and clinics; it listed in Hong Kong in June 2023.
interesting_fact: YSB's platform aggregates long-tail demand from small pharmacies and clinics in lower-tier towns, letting a pharmacy that lacks a drug source it via the platform with delivery in 2-4 days instead of waiting on infrequent local distributor runs.
deep_cut_fact: Zhang was one of the core executives who grew up with SouFun: he served as the property portal's CTO before becoming the vice president running its website, technology, product and mobile operations, spending roughly 15 years there before starting YSB.
notes: No published IR/press email found in this pass; check the contact section of YSB's latest HKEX annual report (hkexnews.hk, stock 9885) for an IR email. Some secondary sources report he graduated in communications engineering in 1997 (Beijing Electronic Science and Technology Institute), unverified here.

name: Spencer Clinton
current_role: Refers to brothers Spencer McCarthy (Chairman & CEO) and Clinton McCarthy (co-founder/Managing Director) of Churchill Living (formerly Churchill Retirement Living), with their father John McCarthy
profile: The Rich List entry 'Spencer, Clinton and John McCarthy' covers the family behind Churchill Living, a privately owned UK retirement-housing developer founded in 1994 by brothers Spencer and Clinton McCarthy. Their father John McCarthy co-founded retirement-housing pioneer McCarthy & Stone in 1963. Churchill, renamed Churchill Living in 2024, manages 250+ retirement developments; Spencer is chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: The business began in 1994 as Emlor Homes building stone and thatched cottages in Hampshire, Dorset and Wiltshire; after the success of its first retirement scheme, Avon Lodge in Southbourne, it switched entirely to retirement apartments in 2000.
deep_cut_fact: The company's very first office was in Clinton McCarthy's garage in the New Forest; in 2016 it became the first retirement specialist to win WhatHouse? 'Housebuilder of the Year' (it had also won in 1998 as Emlor Homes).
notes: Input name 'Spencer Clinton' is a mangled list entry for the McCarthy family (Spencer, Clinton and father John McCarthy). John McCarthy's current status not checked. Family-owned, low-profile; best route is via Churchill Living's head office (Ringwood, Hampshire) contact page.

name: The Sheppard family
current_role: Owners of European Metal Recycling (EMR), via family holding company Ausurus Group; led by chairman/CEO Chris Sheppard
profile: The Sheppard family owns Warrington-based European Metal Recycling, one of the world's largest scrap-metal recyclers with around 160 locations in the UK, Europe and the US. The business began as a family scrap yard in Rochdale in the 1940s, became Sheppard Waste Recovery and The Sheppard Group, and took the EMR name in 1994; Chris Sheppard, son of Phillip Sheppard, now leads it.
interesting_fact: EMR has bolted on plastics recycling (MBA Polymers, 2010) and in 2020 launched 'Our Decade of Action', a 10-year sustainability plan targeting net zero by 2040.
deep_cut_fact: The dynasty began after Winifred Sheppard left wartime London when a bomb destroyed the factory where she worked; with her husband Hubert and their five children she opened the family's first yard, 'The Shed', in central Rochdale.
notes: Famously private family (press has called Chris Sheppard a 'secret billionaire'). Relevant angle: metals recycling, electrification and circular economy. Best route is EMR corporate communications via the website.

name: Shi Jianxiang
current_role: Former chairman of Shanghai Kuailu Investment Group (快鹿集团); resigned April 2016
profile: Shi Jianxiang (施建祥) built Shanghai-based Kuailu Group, a conglomerate spanning taxis, investment/financing platforms, film (it backed 'Ip Man 3') and Hong Kong-listed companies. The group collapsed in 2016 amid a repayment crisis; he left China, resigned as chairman, and Chinese authorities later charged him over illegal fundraising.
notes: NOT a suitable outreach target: he is on China's 'Sky Net' list of 100 most-wanted fugitives (2018) and was reported arrested in the US in Oct 2021 at China's request (sources: https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2021-11-03/1978715.html, https://www.chinatimes.com/realtimenews/20211102000627-260407). Current status after 2021 unknown. No deep-cut or contact recorded.

name: Xia Jun
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Guangdong Create Century Intelligent Equipment Group (创世纪, SZ:300083)
profile: Xia Jun (夏军, b. 1975) has run Shenzhen Create Century Machinery, a maker of CNC machine tools such as drilling/tapping and machining centres used in electronics and auto-parts production, since 2005. The listed company Jinsheng Precision acquired Create Century around 2015-2016 and later refocused on it; Xia became the controlling figure and chairman, and the group was renamed Create Century. He co-holds his stake with Ling Hui.
interesting_fact: Listed company Jinsheng (劲胜), originally a phone-casing maker, bought Create Century to pivot into high-end CNC machine tools; it eventually shed the old business and took Create Century's name, with Xia taking control around 2020.
deep_cut_fact: Xia started out as a salesman (业务员) and later a manager at Zhuhai Beisute (珠海倍速特) enterprise group before becoming executive director and GM of Shenzhen Create Century Machinery in December 2005. He completed an EMBA programme at Tsinghua.
notes: Best route is the board-secretary office (secretary Wu Yongbing) via ir@szccm.com. 2026 press coverage includes a patent dispute and a CSRC Guangdong warning letter on disclosure; avoid those topics.

name: Cai Bo
current_role: Board Secretary and Overseas Market Department Manager, Shenzhen T&S Communications (太辰光, SZ:300570)
profile: Cai Bo (蔡波, b. 1972) is a long-time executive and member of the controlling shareholder group of Shenzhen T&S Communications, a maker of passive optical interconnect components (ceramic ferrules, MT ferrules, high-density MPO connectivity) used in hyperscale and AI data centers and telecom networks. She joined in 2000 as overseas sales manager and has been board secretary since 2011; her wealth is shared with chairman Zhang Zhimin, her husband.
interesting_fact: T&S's high-density optical connectivity products sell globally into large data centers; its 2025 annual report ties growth to the AI compute build-out and new technologies such as silicon photonics and CPO, a direct link to the podcast's data-center theme.
deep_cut_fact: An English major, Cai taught at a school affiliated with China Zhenhua Group from 1992 to 2000 before joining T&S in December 2000 as its overseas sales manager, building the export business that now dominates its revenue.
notes: As board secretary she personally runs the IR channel, so zqb@china-tscom.com reaches her office directly. English-speaking; strong data-center/optical-interconnect angle.
